newsitem.title: USA: Coda Music cutting 17 jobs to trim costs.
newsitem.headline: Coda Music cutting 17 jobs to trim costs.

text.p: Coda Music Technology Inc said Monday it is implementing significant cost savings measures, including the elimination of 17 positions.
The cost plan is aimed at keeping expenses in line with anticipated growth in 1997.
The reduction will not significantly change the company's priorities for product development, repertoire development and sales and marketing efforts, it said.
Coda said the 3.7 upgrade version of its Finale musical composition softwear production has been released and is selling "very well."
The Vivace computerized personal accompaniment product continues to gain market acceptance, it added. However, the school market for Vivace has grown more slowly than anticipated.

"Management continues to be very enthusiastic about the ultimate success of Vivace, but is committed to managing the business according to more conservative expectations of Vivace's growth in 1997," John Paulson, chairman, said in a statement.

"The cost saving measures will not impede Vivace's new consumer thrust in 1997 nor will it compromise gains made to date in Vivace's dealer channel," added Ron Raup, president. "Furthermore, Finale development continues under full steam in order to insure a timely 1997 upgrade."
Coda Music Technology develops and markets proprietary music technology products.
